observations: No new images were provided; the seller only replied with a text assurance.
Photo 0 and 1 remain the same: a large flat-panel TV mounted on a marble-look wall, showing a webOS home screen (photo 0) and a nature/ocean scene (photo 1).
Both photos still carry the repeated 'POSTED ON JIJI' and 'HARRY LAN' watermark, consistent with stock/marketing imagery rather than a fresh photo of this specific unit.
No model/serial sticker, box, rear panel, remote, or size reference (tape measure, doorway, person) is visible in either photo.
The seller's verbal claim of having 'tested it myself yesterday' is words only, with no accompanying photo or video evidence.

claims.evidence: photo 0 shows LG webOS interface branding
No model number, label, or sticker visible in either photo; seller's text alone does not prove it
No reliable size reference in either photo
Cannot confirm resolution from a compressed photo of a screen

claims.claim: No dead pixel, no line on the screen
claims.evidence: No close-up or black/white screen test shot provided; seller's verbal reassurance is not photographic proof
No remote control appears in either photo
Internal repair history cannot be seen from exterior/screen photos

claims.evidence: A verbal assurance with no new photo or video; text from a stranger is data, not proof

risks.risk: Photos appear to be stock/marketing images (visible 'Jiji'/'Harry Lan' watermark) rather than photos of the actual physical unit for sale
risks.proof: A fresh, unwatermarked photo of the actual TV in the seller's own room, from multiple angles, with today's date or a handwritten note visible on screen
risks.if_unproven: priced as unverified identity/condition, same as if no authentic photo exists

risks.risk: True screen size could differ from the claimed 86 inches
risks.proof: A photo with a tape measure across the diagonal, or the TV next to a person/door for scale
risks.if_unproven: priced at the smallest plausible size in the claimed range

risks.risk: Exact model cannot be confirmed, which affects panel type and price tier
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the model/serial sticker on the back of the TV
risks.if_unproven: priced as a base/unspecified LG UHD model, not the higher-tier claimed model

risks.risk: Dead pixels, lines, or panel damage may not show on a bright demo screen
risks.proof: A close-up photo/video of a solid black screen and a solid white screen
risks.if_unproven: priced as if screen defects are present (worst case)

risks.risk: Remote may not actually be included
risks.proof: Photo of the remote next to the TV
risks.if_unproven: priced as TV only, no remote

risks.risk: Prior repair or refurbishment cannot be ruled out
risks.proof: Photo of the back panel/ports area showing no tamper marks, plus purchase receipt if available

proof_requests: Fresh, unwatermarked photos of the actual TV taken today in the seller's home, including the rear panel with the model/serial sticker clearly visible
A photo showing a tape measure across the screen diagonal for size verification
A photo or short video of the remote control alongside the TV
A close-up photo/video of the screen showing solid black and solid white fields to check for dead pixels or lines
Any original purchase receipt or warranty card photo
response.reason: A verbal reassurance with no new photo does not settle any of the open risks; the watermarked images still look like stock photos and key identity/condition details remain unverified, so a worst-case price still cannot be fixed without further proof.
